ch38.d.show: Real part $\mathrm{Re}\,\psi$, probability density $|\psi|^2$, or both
ch38.d.k0: Central wave number $k_0$ of the components; the momentum is $p = \hbar k_0$
ch38.k.goal.build: Adding plane waves with slightly different wave numbers gives a localised wave packet
ch38.k.goal.move: The packet moves at the group velocity $v_\text{g} = \hbar k_0/m$, the speed of a classical particle with the same momentum
ch38.k.obs.one: One plane wave: $|\psi|^2$ is the same everywhere; the position is completely unknown
ch38.k.obs.more: More components (larger $\Delta k$) make a narrower packet (smaller $\Delta x$)
ch38.k.obs.product: $\Delta x\,\Delta k \approx 1/2$: position and wave number cannot both be narrowed (uncertainty)
ch38.k.obs.group: The packet (|ψ|²) keeps pace with the classical particle; the crests of Re ψ move at half that speed (phase velocity)
ch38.k.obs.spread: Narrower packets spread faster as they move (dispersion of a free particle)
ch38.k.assume.electron: Particle: a free electron in one dimension. $k_0$ = 10 nm⁻¹ means 3.8 eV kinetic energy and 1.16 nm/fs
ch38.k.assume.define: $\Delta x$, $\Delta k$: standard deviations (weighted by $|\psi|^2$ and $a_j^2$). With momentum $p = \hbar k$, $\Delta p = \hbar\,\Delta k$ and $\Delta x\,\Delta p \ge \hbar/2$ (equality for a Gaussian packet). The textbook form $\Delta x\,\Delta p \ge \hbar$ is an order-of-magnitude statement
ch38.k.assume.period: Equally spaced components repeat the packet every 42 nm (finitely many components); $\Delta x$ is taken over one repeat. The stage draws only half a repeat (±21 nm) either side of the packet centre, fading to 0 over the last 3 nm, and leaves out the copies in the neighbouring repeats. For $\Delta x$ > 7 nm (a sixth of the repeat, 1–3 plane waves) $|\psi|^2$ fills the whole repeat and is no packet: it is drawn in full, and $\Delta x$ and $\Delta x\,\Delta k$ read –. On narrow screens $x$ runs from −4 to 24 nm (wide screens −5 to 35 nm)
